strain RU301 has a mutation in a gene located downstream of dctA that affects calcium and magnesium utilization, organic acid transport and LPS biosynthesis.
the gene mutated by Tn5 insertion in strain RU 301 is required for LPS II biosynthesis and for the utilization of organic acids in the absence of elevated calcium or magnesium.
strain RU301 is a mutant in which the LPS is rough and the calcium requirement is elevated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gene mutated by the transposons in strains RU301 and VF39C- 86, and the region contained in cosmid pIJ1848, is required for LPS biosynthesis, for calcium utilization and for nitrogen fixation.
the region of the R. leguminosaum chromosome located downstream of dctA and containing the gene mutated in strain RU 301 is required for the synthesis of LPS and calcium utilization.

strain RU301 is unable to synthesize the O-antigene, has an altered LPS II, requires an elevated concentration of divalent cations for growth on sugars and C4-dicarbolyates, and is unable to fix nitrogen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have cloned a region that is essential for nitrogen-fixation in Rhizobium, and that this region is located downstream of dctA.
there are two different genes required for the synthesis of LPS in R. leguminsoarum, one of which is located in the same region of the genome as dctD and is required for nitrogen fixation.

the gene mutated by Tn5 in R. leguminosaum strain RU301 is not essential for growth on succinic acid or TY but is essential for the synthesis of LPS I and for the ability to nodulate and fix nitrogen.
